video_caption: The video opens with a close-up shot of Aretha Franklin, a dark-skinned woman with her dark hair pulled back, wearing a light-colored collared shirt. She is speaking and subtly gesturing with her right hand, her expression engaged. In the top left corner, a logo reads "BMA BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE." Subtitles at the bottom of the screen state, "Aretha: No money problems, whatsoever. That's Toni Braxton. That's not me." The background is dark and out of focus, with some hints of green foliage. The scene then abruptly cuts to a different clip of Aretha Franklin, who appears slightly older with lighter, possibly graying or highlighted hair, also pulled back. She is wearing a light-colored, possibly off-white or light yellow, top and large, dangling earrings. She looks intensely to her right with a surprised or concerned expression, her mouth slightly open, and points her right arm/hand out of frame to the right. The background is dark and indistinct, possibly an indoor wall or blinds. The "BMA BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" logo remains visible, and the subtitle at the bottom simply reads "Aretha:".

The video segment features multiple clips of Aretha Franklin in different settings and time periods. From 00:07 to 00:10, a younger Aretha with dark, coiffed hair and a light-colored top speaks directly to the camera, gesturing with her right hand; text overlays her dialogue: "Aretha: No because when you have range... You can go from one end of the spectrum to the other." (This refers to her ability to sing in different styles or vocal ranges). From 00:10 to 00:13, an older Aretha with long, curly brown hair and a white, textured jacket is seated in a white armchair on a bright TV studio set decorated for Christmas, facing another woman (Meredith Vieira) who is holding papers; text on screen includes a question: "What is it about Beyonce there because you're a big fan of hers as well." A close-up of the older Aretha follows from 00:13 to 00:16, as she smiles and responds, with text indicating her reply: "Yes, I heard she was a fan of mine." From 00:16 to 00:20, a clip shows Aretha with very short, reddish-blonde hair, heavy green eyeshadow, large geometric earrings, and a yellow top with pronounced shoulder pads, speaking in front of a blurry purple neon sign that spells "Aretha". Lastly, from 00:20 to 00:23, a close-up shows Aretha with short, dark, curled hair, red lipstick, and red earrings, smiling warmly at the camera. A "BM BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" logo is visible in the top left corner throughout all segments.

The video features a montage of Aretha Franklin across different periods of her life, consistently showing the "BM BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" logo in the top left. It opens with a close-up shot of a younger Aretha, with short, dark curly hair, speaking thoughtfully and describing someone as "intelligent, very heavy, fine, and very sexy," set against a blurred green background. This transitions to a more recent interview where Aretha, now with long, wavy blonde and brown hair and wearing a bright yellow top and pearl necklace, is seated on a black couch opposite an interviewer in a white blazer, with a "SHOWBIZ ON LOCATION" banner at the bottom stating, "ARETHA FRANKLIN ON MARIAH CAREY AS NEW 'IDOL' JUDGE: 'I'M HAPPY FOR HER'," along with the "HLN" logo. Aretha smiles, adjusts her hair, and appears amused while engaging in conversation. The text on the banner then updates to "MARIAH CAREY REPORTEDLY TO BE PAID $18 MILLION TO JUDGE 'IDOL' CONTESTANTS." The video concludes with a clip of Aretha, again with short, dark curly hair, wearing a white sweatshirt with "MICHIGAN" printed on it, standing in what looks like a backstage or studio area with metal structures and equipment in the background, smiling and gesturing animatedly as overlaid text quotes her saying, "Leave these old dudes alone, the younger brothers are turning it out!".

The video segment features Aretha Franklin in various interview settings, displaying different outfits and hairstyles. From 0:00 to 0:13, she is shown with dark, curly hair and a dark top, speaking and smiling subtly against a blurry background of yellow flowers. A "BM BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" logo appears in the top left corner. Between 0:13 and 0:17, she appears in a white top with large gold earrings, interacting with a man in a suit, gesturing while looking at him. On-screen text identifies her saying, "Aretha: No, no, no darling, I'm just a baby." (Aretha: No, no, no darling, I'm just a baby), indicating her response to the interviewer. A brief clip at 0:17 shows her with a different hairstyle featuring bangs and a vibrant pink blazer, speaking with a serious expression. This transitions to a shot from 0:18 to 0:21 where she is in a dark, possibly leather, jacket with dark curly hair, speaking earnestly and looking directly at the camera. From 0:21 to 0:23, she is again seen with dark curly hair and a light top, smiling and gesturing with her hand near her face. The final clip, from 0:23 to 0:26, shows her seated at a desk, wearing a purple outfit and a prominent necklace, smiling and making hand gestures while conversing with another woman in a brown jacket.

The video montage features Aretha Franklin across various interviews and appearances, spanning different eras and looks. The "BMA BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" logo is visible in the top left corner throughout. Initially, Aretha, in a dark dress with a floral pattern, is interviewed by a man in a suit, where she confidently declares, "Oh I look wonderful!" (0:09). This is followed by a close-up of her, emotional and wiping her eye with a tissue, while the subtitle "SHE WORKS HARD FOR THE MONEY!" (0:10) appears, quoting a song lyric. She then appears in a white blazer, looking directly at the camera with a slight smile (0:12), and subsequently with reddish hair, wearing a strapless black top, looking assertive while making a gesture with her hand (0:13-0:17). A shift then shows her in a black sequined top, seated in a patterned armchair, engaged in a conversation with Wendy Williams, who is wearing a black and white tweed top with a pearl necklace. Aretha appears to be responding to a comment from Wendy (0:19-0:28), making a dismissive hand gesture and touching her nose as she says, "M-m, no, no, I'm not gullible... You get stupid. I'm not gonna be stupid." The segment concludes with Aretha in a vibrant yellow blazer, smiling widely and clapping her hands (0:29-0:34).

The video opens with a close-up of a Black man wearing glasses, a purple shirt, and a dark suit, speaking and smiling; the text "A" and "BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVES" (partial view) are visible in the top left. He is seen asking a question, prompting a thoughtful, then subtly dismissive, reaction from a Black woman with short, dark, curly hair, wearing a black leather jacket; she glances to her right, touches her hair, and then makes a slight head shake and a knowing smile, indicating she will "pass" on the question. The text "BM BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVES" is clearly visible in the top left during her segments. The scene then transitions to an older clip of a younger Black woman with long, dark, wavy hair and a light pink top, talking and smiling off-camera, followed by a brief cut to another Black woman with medium-length dark hair and a black top, smiling broadly. The video then returns to the woman in the pink top before transitioning to a different older clip of a Black woman with very voluminous, curly dark hair and a light-colored patterned jacket, talking and laughing expressively while leaning forward.

The video features various clips of Aretha Franklin across different periods and settings, interspersed with on-screen text and interview dialogue. Initially, she is seen in a studio, wearing a bright pink top with her hair styled up, smiling and filming with a handheld camcorder while a man in a white shirt and black trousers smiles in the background. The scene shifts to an interview where Aretha, first in a grey sweater and then a black headscarf, seriously discusses her father's sermons, stating, "We don't wanna start off on that note either." She then appears with lighter hair, wearing large earrings and a yellow top, speaking expressively against a backdrop of horizontal blinds, followed by a segment in dark sunglasses, a pink shirt, and a black blazer, talking animatedly. A formal speech shows her with short dark hair, dressed in a white jacket, holding a trophy at a podium with gramophone logos, stating "In 67, young and sassy. In 1994, sassy and classy." Later, she's seen playfully dancing with younger people in a grey sweatshirt and black hat, asserting, "Oh yea, I can hang. I'm the homegirl." The video then shows her with curly brown hair and a white flower, smiling, and then with braided hair and dark sunglasses, holding a microphone at an event. Another interview shows her with short dark hair, red earrings, and a dark blue top, clarifying, "Got me mixed up with somebody else," when asked about "sex or lust." The video concludes with her singing on stage in a black and white jacket, and finally, wearing a black cap and t-shirt, stating in an interview, "My man did last night!" in response to "Who gave you goosebumps?" The "BMA BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" logo is consistently displayed in the top left corner throughout most segments.

The video segment opens with a man in a dark suit, white shirt, and patterned tie, laughing heartily with his head tilted back, shown with the subtitle "Aretha: My man did last night!". This cuts to a woman, likely Aretha Franklin herself, wearing a black shirt and baseball cap, covering her face with her hands, also appearing to laugh or react in amusement, with the same subtitle. The scene then transitions to an interviewer, a woman with blonde hair in a red blazer and a white and black patterned blouse, speaking with a serious expression and gesturing slightly. A "LIVE" graphic is visible in the bottom right corner, and the subtitle reads, "Interviewer: R-E-S-P-E-C-T take out P-C-E." This is followed by a shot of Aretha Franklin, with short dark hair, wearing a yellow blazer over a white top, looking thoughtful or slightly amused, seated against a backdrop of red flowers and green foliage. She says, "Take care of T-C-B." which is clarified by the next subtitle "Aretha: Take care of business." The interviewer returns, asking, "She transcribed it wrong?", to which Aretha Franklin definitively replies, "Yes." The interviewer then explains their misinterpretation, "We thought it meant take out P-C-E to get rest.", and Aretha Franklin strongly refutes this, shaking her head and stating, "No. No." The "BMA BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" logo is consistently present in the top left corner of the frames, except for the interviewer's close-up where it appears in the bottom right, suggesting the clips are from an archived interview.

The video features a montage of Aretha Franklin in various interview settings and a live performance, often with the "BMA BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" logo visible in the top left corner. In the initial scenes, she appears in a yellow blazer, then with longer, curly hair in a light top, speaking about having almost gone "toe to toe" with someone and "giving each other the finger." Later, she's seen with her hair tied back, wearing a brown jacket, discussing rap music, noting "Some of the rap is good, some of it is not good. And some of it is wretched." The scene then shifts to her at a piano, wearing a white shirt and a black embellished vest, stating, "It's wonderful when one is influencing in the degree in which I was. I hear myself, I know when someone has been influenced by me." An interviewer in an orange and pink top asks about her admired artists, to which Franklin, wearing a white top and large hoop earrings, humorously replies, "Hmm... After myself..." The montage concludes with a dim-lit live performance where Franklin, in a sparkly white dress, addresses the audience, saying, "Listen, my dear. My darling, my sweet wonderful one. If these people don't hear this tonight, you won't be hearing..." as she pointedly raises her middle finger.

The video opens with a close-up of a woman with dark skin and short, dark hair, wearing purple eyeshadow, speaking thoughtfully and then smiling slightly while looking off-camera against a dark background. A logo "BMA BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" is visible in the top left corner. The scene then transitions to the same woman, now wearing earrings and with a slightly different hairstyle, speaking and smiling broadly outdoors with a blurry green background. The video then cuts to a stage scene where a woman in a white gown stands at a microphone, singing, flanked by other individuals, possibly a choir or band, under purple and blue stage lights. A circular object, possibly a record or film reel, is partially visible on the right side of the screen.

The video features a compilation of clips of Aretha Franklin. It begins with a split screen, showing Aretha Franklin performing on stage in a light green strapless gown with a band and backup singers, while simultaneously showing a more recent interview where she is wearing a black top. Over these scenes, text appears: "I don't know what that was about. I don't know. I saw some pictures, not very attractive or flattering." (The interviewer asks, "She was backing you up?") Aretha replies, "She was in the background." The scene transitions to a panel interview on "THE VIEW" set, where Aretha Franklin, wearing a blue and white patterned top, is seated with four other women, including Whoopi Goldberg and Joy Behar. They are all laughing as the text states, "Whenever it was, she was skinny." Aretha interjects, "I'm STILL skinny." Another woman comments, "She says she's still skinny." Aretha continues, "Okay, chick's not big enough yet. Oh, right." This is followed by a close-up of Aretha in a black sequined top, smiling.

The video then shows Aretha in a kitchen, wearing a blue sweatshirt and white pants, gesturing while talking, and then slicing food on a counter. Text explains her love for food: "No. I love to eat. So... there's nothing therapeutic about it. I love to eat. And so I like to cook." The next clip shows a different panel interview with four women, including Oprah Winfrey in a purple suit and Patti LaBelle in a grey suit, who are discussing ages. Patti LaBelle says, "I'm 49," and Aretha playfully corrects her, "Patti, you know you're 54. You know you're 54 girl." Patti responds, "No, I'm 55 but I didn't wanna tell nobody." Aretha retorts, "You were 51 this morning." The scene cuts to Aretha sitting on a couch in a black leather jacket over an orange top, her short hair styled up, as she says, "I liked what they did. Okay, great, uh, great gowns, beautiful gowns." Another clip shows Wendy Williams, with long brown hair and multiple necklaces, looking serious, then cuts back to Aretha, who deadpans, "I've been looking at a lot of pictures, you know, and I was saying, 'You were entirely too fat for words.'" She then laughs heartily. The final sequence features a younger Aretha Franklin, with short dark hair and a white top, who smiles and explains, "I gained a few pounds, but I'm using Slim Fast and young men." She then says, "I stopped smoking in January... and um, I gained 50 pounds in the interim. But that's alright. It's um... folks like it." The video concludes with a man with a mustache and bald head, wearing a suit and tie, smiling as the text states, "And the brothers are not complaining!" The "BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" logo remains visible throughout the video.

The video opens with a close-up of a man with a bald head, a mustache, wearing a dark suit and patterned tie, smiling and raising his index finger to his chin as he looks to his left. He is seated in a striped armchair against a patterned wallpaper background. The scene transitions to a woman with dark, curly hair, adorned with a sparkly necklace and earrings, wearing a red top, seated in a striped armchair and looking to her right with a gentle smile and slightly parted lips. This is followed by a shot of another woman with short, dark hair, wearing a dark jacket over a white collared shirt, looking directly at the camera with a subtle smile against a light, plain background. Throughout these segments, a watermark "BM BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" (Black Music Archive) is visible in the top left corner. The video concludes with a black screen, retaining the "BM BLACK MUSIC ARCHIVE" watermark in the top left.
